chunks: And (remember) when We turned to you a company of jinn who listened to the Qur'an, so when they attended it, they said, 'Be silent.' And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.
ai.seo_question: What happened when the jinn listened to the Prophet's recitation of the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This verse, from Surah Al-Ahqaf, highlights the divine validation of the Prophet's mission by demonstrating that even unseen beings, the Jinn, recognized the truth of the Qur'an's recitation. Shia exegetes often emphasize the Jinn's immediate conversion and their role as messengers to their own community, illustrating the universal scope of the Prophet's message. The command to 'be silent' (ansitū) underscores the reverence due to the divine word, a principle frequently cited in discussions of Qur'anic recitation etiquette.
